_comment: Upstream digests for the committed .fabro fork. Regenerate with `just refresh-fork-upstream-pins`; every entry MUST carry a reason. See crates/console-fork-drift-check/src/lib.rs.

files.reason: ABSENT FROM OUR FORK BY CONSTRUCTION. Upstream added a whole `disposition` stage; our workflow.fabro has zero references to it. Adopting it is a graph change, not a file copy. `present_in_fork: false` records that this omission is known, so the gate does not report it as a missing file every run.
DIVERGED only slightly from upstream. Low-risk to sync; not yet reviewed.

DIVERGED. Upstream has grown honest-checks / no-detector-evasion, cohesion-decomposition and verbatim-move rules we have not adopted. Porting them is wanted but is its own reviewed change, not a silent sync.

SYNCED VERBATIM from upstream 2026-08-26 (PR #1872, merged 2026-08-26T01:46:04Z as 1a30cdc8, released in v0.75.1) — the publish stage now proves the remote tip is this run's own prior push and then retries EXACTLY ONCE with `git push --force-with-lease=<assignment-branch>:<observed-tip>`, scoped to the assignment feature branch. A bare `--force` stays forbidden, and a lease mismatch still parks. This supersedes the previous entry's closing promise — 'the retry's exact-match ci.yml scoping is a known upstream wart ... we inherit the fix when they ship it' — which is now DISCHARGED: they shipped it and this is the inheritance. Keep it verbatim: a local 'improvement' to borrowed prose becomes a divergence nobody remembers agreeing to, and this repo VENDORS its copy at the repository root while sibling consumers resolve theirs from the installed plugin cache, so nothing here is inherited automatically — every upstream fix to this file arrives as a deliberate sync like this one.

DELIBERATELY NOT SYNCED, same reason as review.md — and upstream has additionally rewritten it to consume a `disposition` record that our graph does not produce, so syncing it alone would reference a stage we do not run.

DELIBERATELY NOT SYNCED. This repo's review gate is ADVISORY / ship-on-cap by recorded decision (workflow.fabro, work-item bd-ib-egms32); upstream's is BLOCKING by default. Syncing would silently revert a ratified policy. Re-pin on upstream change only after confirming the change is policy-neutral.

DIVERGED, and the divergence is itemised by design review. This is the file the fork exists to own; treat any upstream movement here as a design review, never a sync. (1) REVIEW GATE = NO LONGER ADVISORY; THE 2026-08-22 'KEEP' DECISION IS SUPERSEDED 2026-08-26 (livespec-console-beads-fabro-7zq3lg, PR #844). The superseded entry read: our graph keeps the ADVISORY ship-on-cap gate while upstream moved its default to BLOCKING, 'the advisory form is this repo's ratified policy', 'do not re-litigate on a future drift unless upstream's rationale itself changes.' THAT PREMISE WAS FALSE and is the reason the decision did not survive: the advisory form was never RATIFIED anywhere. SPECIFICATION/spec.md says the opposite -- it names ship-on-cap as one of the auto-dispositions 'a setting enables', and requires the orchestrator to escalate to a human 'every decision no setting may auto-dispose'. scenarios.md separately describes an operator setting a per-item merge_on_review_cap override against a false global default and expecting it to govern. An unconditional ship-on-cap conforms to neither. So the gate is now conditioned on merge_on_review_cap_outcome, the review fallthrough moved from `pr` to `escalate` (the graph fails CLOSED), and this is CONFORMANCE with the ratified spec rather than adoption of an upstream default. RECORDED HONESTLY: the change was made before this pin entry was read, and its original justification -- that the console had newly begun surfacing the merge_on_review_cap dial -- was WRONG on the dates. That dial landed 2026-07-16 (dce254f) and the spec scenario 2026-07-14 (b23e8b4), both over a month BEFORE the 2026-08-22 review that chose KEEP. The 2026-08-22 review therefore had the dial in front of it. The change stands on the spec clauses above, which are stronger grounds than the ones first given, not on the new-information claim. (2) JANITOR WORKFLOW-DRIFT GATE = PORTED 2026-08-22: the janitor node runs `just check-no-workflow-edits check`, matching upstream. (3) pr_adapter TIER SPLIT = PORTED 2026-08-22. (4) C5 DEAD-IMPLEMENTER CIRCUIT BREAKER = PORTED 2026-08-25: implementation_diff gate plus dead_implementer terminal, failing closed before janitor/review spend; script lines byte-identical to upstream because the LIVESPEC_DEAD_IMPLEMENTER sentinel is the Dispatcher-facing contract. OMISSION UNCHANGED: our graph still omits upstream's disposition stage, so review -> review_fix is direct where upstream routes review -> disposition. NOT ADOPTED: upstream's review_fix_visit_cap input; this fork keeps its own hardcoded two-fix-round edge guard, and changing the round count is a separate decision from making the safety dial real. (5) RE-PINNED 2026-08-26 to 397bdb7124b8 after reviewing upstream's ONLY substantive change to this file in that movement: the three implementer nodes' acp.command moved from the shared `{{ inputs.acp_adapter }}` to per-node `implement_adapter` / `fix_adapter` / `review_fix_adapter`, plus comment rewording. NOT PORTED, and this is a SUPPORTED SHAPE rather than a lag: the Dispatcher resolves each node's adapter through NODE_INPUT_CANDIDATES (commands/_acp_node_adapters.py), which lists the per-node input FIRST and the shared acp_adapter SECOND precisely so BOTH graph shapes resolve, and whose own comment states it 'reads what the workflow ACTUALLY declares rather than assuming a shape, so a not-yet-migrated target is never sent an --input name its own workflow does not define -- which fabro would reject outright'. This fork keeps the shared input at all three nodes and dispatches continue to bind acp_adapter. Adopting the split would buy per-node model configurability and nothing else -- upstream's defaults for the three are deliberately IDENTICAL, so the split changed the surface and not the behaviour -- so it is a separate optional improvement, not a correctness gap.

DIVERGED: this Rust console fork deliberately pins the Rust-capable `python-rust-agent-` sandbox image, while upstream pins the Python-only `python-agent-` image. The fork-drift gate normalizes exactly that upstream docker value before hashing workflow.toml, so upstream docker tag bumps no longer require re-review; every other upstream byte in workflow.toml remains pinned and must still be reviewed or ported. RE-PINNED 2026-08-26 to 397bdb7124b8; the preceding re-pin at a7d9c88ef0a4 reviewed four upstream changes (livespec-console-beads-fabro-7zq3lg carries the detail). NOT PORTED, each with a reason: (a) upstream's new `disposition_adapter` input -- this fork has no disposition node, and all four `disposition` occurrences in our workflow.fabro are prose in comments and diagnostic strings with zero graph references, matching the standing prompts/disposition.md pin; (b) upstream's new `review_fix_visit_cap` input -- this fork deliberately hardcodes that bound as an edge guard on review's own visit count, because a max_visits would hard-abort (VisitLimitExceeded) on the very visit that should ship; (c) upstream's implementer-model pin on `acp_adapter` (Opus 5 + high effort) -- the Dispatcher overrides that input at dispatch time anyway, so the fork default is only reached by a bare `fabro run`, and porting it would carry an unmet acceptance obligation upstream itself records (old adapter versions silently ignored the model env and defaulted to Haiku, so the resolved model must be verified in a run transcript, not asserted from the adapter string). (d) WAS a known behavioural divergence and is now RESOLVED -- recorded rather than deleted so the correction is not lost. Upstream gates its ship-on-review-cap edge on merge_on_review_cap_outcome; this fork's review -> pr edge was CONDITIONLESS and therefore always shipped on cap, while the console's own Settings surface exposed merge_on_review_cap (default false), so the displayed dial was the inverse of what ran. PR #844 (merge f688d5b1) conditioned that edge and moved the review FALLTHROUGH from `pr` to `escalate`, so the graph now fails CLOSED and the dial is truthful end to end. See the workflow.fabro pin's entry (1) for why that change rests on SPECIFICATION/spec.md's setting-enables and escalate-otherwise clauses rather than on upstream's default. (e) upstream's per-node adapter split (acp_adapter -> implement_adapter / fix_adapter / review_fix_adapter) = NOT ADOPTED, backward compatible by upstream's explicit design; the detail is on the workflow.fabro pin's entry (5). Note (c) above names acp_adapter, which upstream has since renamed; that decision is unchanged and now reads against upstream's implement_adapter default.
